name: Hello World Computer
description: An onchain neural network that learns from yes/no questions, training one shared perceptron from paid answers.
about:
## A mind built from yes and no

The Hello World Computer is an onchain neural network — a single shared perceptron that starts knowing nothing. Everything it comes to lean toward, someone taught it through yes-or-no questions.

## Asking and answering

Anyone can ask a question for a flat 0.01 ETH fee. Each question is deployed as its own *Binary* contract and joins a queue. People answer questions yes or no by attaching ETH — the more ETH, the more weight the answer carries (minimum 0.0001 ETH per answer). While a question waits in line, every answer it receives raises its standing.

## The lifecycle

Roughly every 10 minutes the highest-activity question in the queue is promoted into the live set. Up to 150 questions can be live at once and the queue holds up to 2,048. A live question stays active for about 25 hours. Anyone can call `push()` to move the machine forward: it settles the oldest live question that has finished its run, then promotes the next one. Whoever triggers a promotion earns a small 0.0001 ETH bounty.

## Learning and payouts

When a question settles, its accumulated answer fees are split 90% to the question's creator and 10% to the protocol, and the question teaches the shared perceptron exactly once — nudging the computer's 1,024 feature weights toward the net yes/no lean it received. You can read the whole mind at any time with `featureStates()`, or ask it what it makes of a new message with `ask()`.

## Payments are pull-based

Creator cuts, promotion bounties, and protocol cuts accumulate as pending balances. Call `withdraw()` to collect what the computer owes you. The contract has no owner controls, no upgrade path, and no pause — the rules are fixed at deployment.
risks: Asking a question costs exactly 0.01 ETH — sending any other amount reverts.
A new question is not immediately live. It sits in a queue and is promoted roughly every 10 minutes, highest-activity first. The queue holds at most 2,048 questions and reverts when full.
A live question only settles (paying out fees and teaching the mind) after its ~25-hour active lifetime, once someone calls push().
Answer fees are split 90% to the question's creator and 10% to the protocol at settlement.
Payouts are pull-based: creator cuts, promotion bounties, and protocol cuts accumulate as pending balances you must withdraw yourself.
The contract accepts plain ETH transfers only from its own question contracts; direct sends from any other address revert.
No admin keys, no upgradeability, no pause — the rules are fixed at deployment.

deployBinary.title: Ask a Question
deployBinary.description: Ask the computer a question for a flat 0.01 ETH fee, deploying it as its own Binary contract that joins the queue.

fields.label: Question
fields.description: The yes/no question to ask. Its words are reduced to features the computer can learn from.

deployBinary.warning: Costs exactly 0.01 ETH — any other amount reverts. The question enters a queue and only goes live once promoted (roughly every 10 minutes, highest-activity first).

question.label: Question
question.description: The yes/no question to ask. Its words are reduced to features the computer can learn from.

batchAnswer.title: Answer Questions
batchAnswer.description: Answer one or more questions yes or no in a single transaction, sending ETH equal to the sum of each answer's weight.
batchAnswer.warning: The ETH you send must exactly equal the sum of all answer weights, and every target must be a question deployed by this computer, or the whole batch reverts.

answers.label: Answers
answers.description: A list of answers, each a (question address, yes/no, ETH weight) triple. Minimum 0.0001 ETH per answer.

push.title: Advance the Computer
push.description: Advance the computer one step: settle the oldest expired live question and promote the top queued one when due.
push.warning: Whoever triggers a promotion earns a 0.0001 ETH bounty. If nothing is due to settle or promote, the call simply does nothing.

ask.title: Read the Mind
ask.description: Run a message through the trained perceptron to see which way it leans and its confidence — a read-only query.

fields.label: Message
fields.description: Any text to classify against what the computer has learned.

message.label: Message
message.description: Any text to classify against what the computer has learned.

confidence.label: Confidence margin
confidence.description: How strongly the computer leans, as a signed margin. Larger magnitude means a stronger conviction.

featureStates.title: Feature Weights
featureStates.description: The computer's full mind: 1,024 signed perceptron weights in feature order, raw as stored, readable in a single call.

totalBinaries.title: Total Questions
totalBinaries.description: How many questions have ever been asked.

totalResponses.title: Lessons Learned
totalResponses.description: How many times the computer has learned something — one lesson per settled question that carried a non-zero lean.

totalAnswers.title: Total Votes
totalAnswers.description: The total yes and no answer weight cast across every question.

pendingWithdrawals.title: Pending Balance
pendingWithdrawals.description: How much ETH the computer is holding for an address — creator cuts, bounties, or protocol cuts — awaiting withdrawal.

withdraw.title: Withdraw
withdraw.description: Collect everything the computer owes you: creator cuts, promotion bounties, and any protocol cuts.

artifact.title: Artwork Address
artifact.description: The address of the computer's one-of-one artwork contract.

owner.title: Artwork Owner
owner.description: The current owner of the computer's one-of-one artwork, who also receives the 10% protocol cut.

currentOffer.title: Artwork Offer
currentOffer.description: The artwork's current sale offer, if any. Delegates to the artwork contract.

onAnswer.title: On Answer (internal)
onAnswer.description: Internal hook, callable only by the computer's own questions, that records an answer against a queued or live question.

BinaryDeployed.title: Question Asked
BinaryDeployed.description: Emitted when a new question is asked and enters the queue.

BinaryActivated.title: Question Went Live
BinaryActivated.description: Emitted when a queued question is promoted into the live set.

BinarySettled.title: Question Settled
BinarySettled.description: Emitted when a live question finishes its run: its fees are split 90/10 and its lean is taught to the mind.

weight.label: Learned lean
weight.description: The question's net yes/no lean taught to the perceptron (signed).

Taught.title: Computer Taught
Taught.description: Emitted when a settled question teaches the shared perceptron a lesson.

ArtifactDeployed.title: Artwork Deployed
ArtifactDeployed.description: Emitted once at construction, when the companion one-of-one artwork is deployed.

IncorrectDeployFee.title: Incorrect Fee
IncorrectDeployFee.description: Asking a question requires sending exactly 0.01 ETH.

OnlyBinary.title: Only a Question
OnlyBinary.description: This action may only be performed by one of the computer's own question contracts.

QueueFull.title: Queue Full
QueueFull.description: The queue is at its maximum of 2,048 waiting questions. Try again after some have been promoted.

NotAnswerable.title: Not Answerable
NotAnswerable.description: The question is no longer accepting answers — only queued or live questions can be answered.

AnswerValueMismatch.title: Value Mismatch
AnswerValueMismatch.description: The ETH sent does not equal the sum of the answer weights in the batch.

InsufficientFunds.title: Nothing to Withdraw
InsufficientFunds.description: There is no pending balance to withdraw for your address.

FundsTransfer.title: Transfer Failed
FundsTransfer.description: An ETH transfer failed. Ensure your address can receive ETH.
